## 席位 ACCEPT · head `3c52359aad959967e72e2dd5d9ef0cb08f556c69`

#31739 PR-3a (register an AI service account and mint its key). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, changeset `patch`. The paths give no review face, so the seat reviewed it at TIER_DEFAULT. It is not governed, and it is 2135 lines.

- **Who reaches the doors.** Both routes read the caller only from the better-auth session, so an API key never reaches them. Anonymous gets 401, and a held session gets 403 with its posture before either handler runs.
  - Register admits an org admin or owner of the current organization (`isOrgAdminGrade` within the validity window), or a platform admin.
  - Create-key admits the account's accountable owner (who must still be a member of the account's organization), an admin of that organization, or a platform admin.
  - A person's id answers 404 as unknown. A retired account (no membership) gets 409. An unreadable membership or policy answers 503, never 403.
- **What register writes.** The `sys_user` row is born with kind `agent` through the data engine, so the row rules and every `sys_user` hook judge it (D1, D7). Its one membership is added as plain `member` through the vendor's `addMember` in the same unit of work, and a refused membership rolls the row back. The owner must be a member of the organization today.
- **What create-key writes.** `active_organization_id` is the account's own organization, never the caller's or the body's. The key is signed by the shared rule (`readRequestedApiKeyExpiry` and `signApiKeyExpiry` in core), so a person's key and an account's key carry the same default life and ceiling. The key is generated only after every check. The raw secret is returned once, and an insert failure never echoes the row.
- **`POST /keys` is unchanged.** It is a pure move into the core rule, and the ceiling keeps its ledgered `API_KEY_EXPIRY_TOO_LONG`.
- **Accepted deviation:** the account door answers the ceiling as `VALIDATION_FAILED` on `expires_at`, because the runtime's code is not plugin-auth's to raise.
- **PR-2 carry-ins, done.** An AI service account is never counted as an administrator by the last-admin guard, and never an upgrade-report recipient or a wall-audit administrator. Both read the found ids once more by id and drop the agent rows. Both are pinned.
- **Display gate.** The `sys_user` actions' `visible` is display-only, and the doors judge the caller themselves. There is no `ai` block, so both actions stay human-only.
- **Evidence (thread report):**
  - dispatch-gates: 109 of 109 ran, all exit 0.
  - The five package suites and test-typecheck are green, and eslint is clean.
  - The whole dogfood package passed under the lock: 443 files, 3677 tests, including the new HTTP file for both doors.
  - All 7 ablations went red and were restored.
- **Open debt, recorded on #31739:** there is no purpose column ("the name carries the purpose for now"). Lifecycle doors come in 3b (`Fixes #31739`).

Landing: the merge base is 22 first-parent commits behind main, so the dev thread merges main locally and pushes, because a relay update-branch runs no CI. The seat then confirms the merge-only delta. Once CI is all green, the seat relays `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.

## 席位 ACCEPT · head `e300def51c995ad228c18b65230bb29b6eb6ef91`

A merge-only delta of ACCEPT 6746057649 (head 3c52359a). The merge e300def5 brings main c72ec196 onto 3c52359a.

- **The PR's own diff is unchanged.** Outside the generated tenant-audit census, the net diff against main is identical before and after the merge: the same hunks, still 31 files and +2056/−79.
- **The one conflict was the generated census**, `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and its counts file. Main's version was taken, regenerated with `tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, and the page figures were moved to match: 284 → 286 write sites, 202 of 286 decidable and 84 not, 115 elevation-undecidable, 76 const-named, and 161 of 286 = 56%. The census check and its self-test are green. These are counts, with no claim changed.
- **Evidence on this head:**
  - Suites: core, runtime, plugin-auth, plugin-security and platform-objects passed, with `check:test-typecheck` in all five.
  - Dogfood: the 7 dogfood files that exercise these doors and the admin and route registries passed (105 tests).
  - dispatch-gates: 109 of 109 exit 0, and `--ran` reconciled.
- It is not governed and is 2135 lines.

Landing: when CI is all green, the seat relays `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.

### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **66** documentable anchor(s).

**68** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 50 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 45 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 50 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **73** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6be38fa7870bf4395fe751f3301130c6b12ea902` — the merge of head `e300def51c995ad228c18b65230bb29b6eb6ef91` into base `01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6be38fa7870bf4395fe751f3301130c6b12ea902 && git checkout 6be38fa7870bf4395fe751f3301130c6b12ea902
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3 e300def51c995ad228c18b65230bb29b6eb6ef91 && git checkout -B drift-repro 01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3 && git merge --no-ff e300def51c995ad228c18b65230bb29b6eb6ef91

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 01559b80d5b580ca55a8c79b71d501a480b956d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.
